contests.districtDescription: Rio Grande Valley — Brownsville to Corpus Christi (post-2025 redistricting: Hidalgo County portion removed, Nueces County / Corpus Christi area added)
contests.raceRatingNotes: Cook moved from Lean Republican to Toss-up (Jan 15, 2026). Sabato's Crystal Ball also rates Toss-up (moved from Lean Republican after apparent Democratic rebound with Latino voters). Inside Elections: Toss-up. District PVI shifted dramatically under 2025 Republican gerrymander from D+16 to approximately D+1; Trump carried the new district lines by ~10 pts in 2024 vs. Biden +3 in 2020.
contests.redistrictingNotes: 2025 Texas mid-decade Republican gerrymander removed Hidalgo County Democratic base and added Corpus Christi / Nueces County Republican-leaning territory. Supreme Court allowed the new map to proceed (Dec 2025). District is majority-Latino but trending Republican in presidential voting.

candidates.notes: Incumbent U.S. Rep. for TX-34 since 2023 (previously served TX-15 2017-2023 before switching districts). Won 2024 general vs. Mayra Flores 51%-49%. McAllen-based attorney. Running for re-election; announced reelection bid with focus on education, Social Security/Medicare, and South Texas job creation. Faces a much tougher district after 2025 gerrymander.

First-generation Mexican-American from Brownsville. Holds PhD in public policy from RAND (Pardee RAND Graduate School), postdoctoral fellow at Princeton. Works as public policy researcher and musician. Self-described democratic socialist. Ran on universal healthcare, childcare, campaign finance reform, border cooperation over militarization. Raised only ~$33K vs. Gonzalez's $1.9M — not a serious electoral threat to the incumbent.

keyEndorsements: Multiple candidates dropped out and coalesced behind Flores after Trump endorsement
candidates.notes: U.S. Army veteran and Texas Army National Guard member; former assistant U.S. Attorney for Southern District of Texas. Emphasized landmark prosecutions of cartel-connected and human trafficking operations. Announced July 2025. Received Trump endorsement in December 2025, causing several other GOP candidates to drop out or consolidate support behind him. No relation to Mayra Flores. Campaign focuses on border security, veterans issues, economy, and anti-cartel enforcement record.

Former U.S. Rep. for TX-34 (Jun 2022 – Jan 2023): first Mexican-born woman elected to Congress, won 2022 special election. Lost TX-34 general to Gonzalez in Nov 2022, then ran against Gonzalez again in 2024 in TX-34 and lost 49%-51%. Third consecutive campaign for the same seat. Born in Burgos Tamaulipas, Mexico; U.S. citizen; respiratory therapist background. Previously served on Homeland Security and Agriculture Committees. Switched from TX-28 (where she briefly considered running) to TX-34 in Aug 2025. Despite Trump backing rival Eric Flores, she has remained in the race, arguing she has the highest name recognition and proven vote totals in the district. This is the headline 'Flores vs. Flores' primary matchup.

Retail leadership professional. Campaigns on faith-based governance, pro-life stance, and traditional family values. Raised $152K — third-highest among GOP primary field, well behind the two Floreses but meaningfully above the remaining field. Included as the only other Republican with a credible (though long-shot) fundraising base. No campaign website confirmed.

ballotMeasuresNotes: No statewide Texas ballot measures confirmed for November 3, 2026 general election as of this research date (Feb 27, 2026). The March 3, 2026 primary ballots contain non-binding party propositions (10 Republican, 13 Democratic) but these are internal party advisory questions, not official ballot measures. Texas constitutional amendments for 2026 were not identified from available sources — the legislature adjourned in June 2025 and may have placed measures on the ballot; check Ballotpedia Texas 2026 ballot measures page for updates.
